Author: Rajesh Bindal
Bench: Rajesh Bindal
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No.163 Of 2015
 The State Of Rajasthan Appel
 Versus
 Sanjay & Anr. Res
 O R D E R
We have heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant and the respondents.

The appeal has been directed only against the acquittal rendered for the offences punishable under Sections 366A and 376(2)
(g) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, the IPC) while maintaining the conviction rendered under Sections 363 and 511 of the IPC.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellant-State submitted that the evidence of the prosecutrix was not duly taken into consideration by the High Court.
The Trial Court has taken note of the aforesaid fact in rendering the conviction.
Thus, the impugned judgment required interference.
However, as rightly observed by the High Court, the medical report of the prosecutrix does not suggest the commission of the offences punishable under Sections 366A and 376(2)(g) of the IPC.
Reason: In the absence of any concrete material, the High Court has correctly convicted the respondents only for the offences punishable under Sections 363 and 511 of the IPC.
Thus, we are not inclined to interfere with the impugned order.
The appeal is dismissed accordingly.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
